title: LumenForge - Hybrid Marketplace Connector & Listing Ops Design Huddle
meeting_header: Date: 2027-09-03 | Time: 15:00 PT | Duration: 52 minutes | Attendees: Eli Navarro (Redwood AE), Priya Reddy (Redwood SE), Nina Brooks (Redwood Solutions), Martin Kline (LumenForge CTO), Sara Velez (Platform Lead), Diego Ramos (Security Eng), Ruth Yang (SRE)
summary: Technical working session to align on hybrid marketplace connector design for LumenForge listing. Covered VPC/private connector flow, KMS/HSM compatibility, helm operator packaging, SBOM and image signing, telemetry and billing hooks, and an end-to-end pilot plan. Action items agreed for repo access, runbook, and SOC2/network artifacts.
topics: VPC peering and private connector flow
Helm operator packaging and upgrade path
Telemetry, billing metering, and SBOM/image signing
next_steps: Redwood to share connector prototype repo and sample Helm chart by 2027-09-10
LumenForge to provide SOC2 report and network diagram by 2027-09-09
Schedule follow-up bench test (throughput + cold start) week of 2027-09-20
action_items: Eli Navarro - Share connector prototype repo and sample Helm chart - 2027-09-10
Priya Reddy - Draft end-to-end runbook for VPC peering, private control plane and fallback policy - 2027-09-15
Martin Kline - Provide LumenForge OCI image signing policy and SBOM expectations - 2027-09-09
Diego Ramos - Confirm KMS/HSM vendor and send HSM compatibility checklist - 2027-09-11
transcript:
[00:00] Eli Navarro: All right, everyone, thanks for joining. We know time is tight so we'll try to get through the connector flow and the listing checklist. um Priya and Nina from Redwood here, and Martin, Sara, Diego, Ruth — thanks
[00:08] Martin Kline: Yeah thanks, Eli. we wanna make sure this marketplace listing doesn't force us to expose any customer data. we're looking at a hybrid model - some traffic through Redwood hosted inference, some routed to our on-prem nodes.
[00:20] Priya Reddy: Right, and today we'll go over two main paths: hosted + private connector (VPC peering) and a fully private on-prem bundle with our helm operator. We'll call the private connector the "bridge" flow for the call.
[00:34] Sara Velez: Quick note — our timeline is tight: procurement wants something in the marketplace by EoQ. ideally a draft listing by the middle of next month.
[00:42] Nina Brooks: Got it. Can you confirm which clouds you need first — AWS only or multi-cloud?
[00:48] Martin Kline: Primarily AWS in APAC and EU, but we want an Azure listing later and GCP maybe Q1.
[00:55] Diego Ramos: Security first: we need full KMS integration, image signing, and a verified SBOM. Also SSO/SAML for console access.
[01:04] Eli Navarro: Understood — Redwood Private supports KMS integrations and we have an HSM flow; we'll detail the keywrap process. quick caveat: there are slight differences between our managed KMS flow and customer-managed HSM that can affect cold-start latency.
[01:18] Martin Kline: Can you explain that a bit? cold start latency matter for us since we have interactive sessions.
[01:24] Priya Reddy: Sure — in managed flow we keep a warm key cache and the KV cache accessible so we don't roundtrip to HSM on every request. with HSM-backed keys the key exchange is more involved — sometimes we do an auth step at pod start which can add a second or two on cold starts. also transcription: sometimes KMS gets reported as "K-M-S" in logs, just FYI.
[01:44] Ruth Yang: hmm okay. acceptable if there is a documented SLA and a warmup plan. we can run a probe to keep a tiny pool of pods warm during business hours.
[01:52] Priya Reddy: Exactly. We recommend a small warm pool and keep-alive ping for low tail-latency. also we have an autoscale policy that can do predictive scale for scheduled bursts.
[02:03] Sara Velez: About the helm operator and upgrades — we need zero-downtime upgrades across clusters. what's Redwood's approach for operator upgrades and migration?
[02:12] Nina Brooks: Our helm operator supports canary upgrades and side-by-side deploys. we ship a CRD versioning guide in the repo. caveat: CRD migration requires DB migration steps for older private installs; we'll flag that in the runbook.
[02:26] Martin Kline: Are there any customer-facing agent components that would run in our cluster? we prefer minimal surface area.
[02:32] Priya Reddy: Minimal — typically a small connector daemonset and the helm operator. the heavy model runtime remains either in Redwood Dedicated or in your private nodes depending on the deployment pattern. the connector manages control-plane talk, credential exchange, and optional prefix/KV cache replication.
[02:47] Diego Ramos: On credentials — we want to use our KMS and not hand keys to Redwood. is key sharing required?
[02:53] Eli Navarro: No sharing required. We support customer-managed KMS via an envelope key approach. Redwood holds a wrapped envelope key, but the unwrapping requires a call to your KMS. we can also support HSM VPN for customers who need airgapped key ops.
[03:10] Martin Kline: Sounds good. whats the path for image signing and SBOM?
[03:14] Nina Brooks: We integrate with common signing tools — cosign or sigstore. Repo will include example pipeline for CI that produces SBOM and attaches signatures. Marketplace listing requires the signed image and SBOM attached to the listing metadata or a reachable artifact URL.
[03:28] Sara Velez: For the listing, do we need to publish a public image or can it be private behind a registry with access tokens?
[03:34] Priya Reddy: Both options supported. For AWS marketplace we often do a private ECR offering with account-registered access, but for Azure gallery you might need an image in a specific registry configuration. We'll provide docs per marketplace.
[03:48] Diego Ramos: Telemetry — we need to ensure no PII leaves our cluster, and billing metrics should be tokenized. how does Redwood's meter work?
[03:56] Eli Navarro: Redwood meter exports per-route token counts and per-model cost attribution. For private or hybrid flows we can run a local metering shim that reports aggregated usage without message-level payloads — only token counts and model IDs. that meets many compliance needs.
[04:12] Ruth Yang: Excellent. and audit logs? we require immutable audit trails for admin actions.
[04:18] Priya Reddy: Private deploy includes an audit log sink and optional Kinesis/CloudWatch or S3 archival. For on-prem we can ship a local collector. Logs are timestamped and signed for integrity; there is sometimes a mismatch in the field names across clouds in auto transcripts but we map those in the ingestion layer.
[04:36] Martin Kline: Ok let's talk about routing — we want to keep low-latency inference for EU customers. If capacity on our private nodes drops, can Redwood route to hosted low-tier models automatically?
[04:46] Eli Navarro: Yes, Smart routing supports policy-based fallback. you can set priority: private cluster first, then dedicated reserved pool, then hosted. For EU latency we recommend a regional dedicated pool in eu-west-1 as fallback to avoid cross-region hops.
[04:59] Sara Velez: Are there cost implications for fallback? we need clear unit economics in contract.
[05:04] Eli Navarro: It'll be costed separately; Redwood Optimize can produce a forecast with expected token counts per route. we'll include a sample forecast in the commercial pack.
[05:14] [Crosstalk] Diego Ramos: (inaudible) ... how do we validate network egress ports?
[05:19] Priya Reddy: We'll send a network checklist with required egress ranges, ports, and DNS endpoints — typical ports 443 outbound, with TLS mutual auth for control-plane.
[05:29] Martin Kline: One more technical question — KV cache replication. We saw notes about prefix caching. do you replicate KV cache to our cluster for locality?
[05:38] Nina Brooks: We support optional prefix/KV sync. For hybrid flow we replicate a small subset of the KV cache (embedding index and recent tokens) to the connector to speed up local hits. tradeoff is eventual consistency and extra bandwidth during sync windows.
[05:52] Eli Navarro: Also note that KV cache replication may affect our dedup and cache eviction heuristics; we'll include ttl and size tuning knobs in the operator CRD.
[06:03] Sara Velez: Great. let's discuss the POC bench — what metrics should we capture in a pilot?
[06:09] Priya Reddy: Throughput (tokens/s), p95 and p99 tail latency, cold-start distribution, cost per 1k tokens per route, and failover recovery time. We'll provide a bench harness and sample scripts.
[06:21] Martin Kline: We'll also want to run a privacy check — replay synthetic prompt set and validate no data gets sent to hosted endpoints.
[06:29] Eli Navarro: We can run that; Redwood has a privacy harness to redact payloads and only report aggregated counts. we'll add that to the pilot runbook.
[06:38] Diego Ramos: On compliance docs — can Redwood provide SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation plus penetration test reports?
[06:44] Eli Navarro: Yes. We will share SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 artifacts under NDA, plus latest pentest summary. we'll put links in a shared drive.
[06:53] Martin Kline: Who owns the support escalation matrix during pilot and post-listing?
[06:58] Nina Brooks: Redwood CSM will own day-to-day pilot ops; AE/SE will handle technical escalations. We'll share on-call rotations and a Slack channel.
[07:08] Eli Navarro: Ok quick recap and next steps — we'll share connector prototype repo and helm chart by Friday next week, runbook by 9/15, and LumenForge shares SOC2 and registry policies by 9/9. schedule bench for week of 9/20.
[07:24] Sara Velez: Sounds good. Also please include a checklist for marketplace metadata fields (logos, data residency tags, pricing tiers).
[07:31] Priya Reddy: We'll add that.
[07:33] [00:07:33] Martin Kline: Thanks, this was helpful.
[07:36] [00:07:36] Eli Navarro: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with the repo link and the runbook timeline.
[07:40] [END]"
